title: Designing a FINRA for Frontier AI
note: Institute for Progress design paper. Membership at 10^26 FLOP, CAISI spin-out, board composition, examination-led enforcement. No record retention clause found.

title: A Pragmatic Approach to AI Governance in America
note: FARO concept — annual procedural audit, pre-release attestation, auditor document access limited to model-card-type materials.

title: Anthropic's Advanced AI Framework
note: Covered-entity criteria 10^25 FLOP + revenue test; six-monthly risk reports; the evaluator retention-prohibition clause quoted in the article body.

title: OpenAI's Frontier Governance Framework
note: Addresses California TFAIA and the EU GPAI Code of Practice. Safety/security model reports; 30-day changelog on framework changes. No retention period clause found.

title: A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age
note: Names FINRA explicitly as the model; board composition, industry funding, voluntary 30-day pre-release submission, quarterly benchmark refresh. No compute threshold, no retention clause. See also the same-day Axios interview at https://www.axios.com/2026/07/14/demis-hassabis-ai-regulation-google-deepmind

title: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google are working to create an AI standards body

title: Outsider Oversight: Designing a Third Party Audit Ecosystem for AI Governance
note: arXiv:2206.04737. Five-axis institutional design split (Sec. 3); audit-access and self-audit-indistinguishability findings (Sec. 3, Table 1); IP counter-argument and NIST example (Sec. 4.3.2); HireVue case (Sec. 4.3); limitations on choosing a reform path and axis interaction (Sec. 5). Main comparator is the PCAOB; does not address FINRA directly.

title: Closing the AI Accountability Gap: Defining an End-to-End Framework for Internal Algorithmic Auditing
